chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both,
He said: Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, has made for the woman the patience of ten men. And when she becomes pregnant, He adds to her the strength [patience] of ten other men.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of women's patience in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to highlight the superior spiritual and physical endurance of women, a concept often discussed in Shia tafsir and fiqh regarding their capacity for worship and hardship. The doubling of this 'patience' during pregnancy underscores the unique divine grace bestowed upon mothers, linking their biological role to heightened spiritual resilience. This hadith serves as a counter-narrative to cultural perceptions of female fragility, affirming their significant status in the cosmic order.
